quotes.text: Radar operates on a per-charge level
enable **Use Radar on payment methods saved for future use**.

findings: May and November say some Stripe Radar model inputs are automatic and others come from the merchant's integration. Payment Links, Checkout, Elements and mobile SDKs collect signals such as device information and IP. Direct integrations typically send client IP/user agent/checkout URL on PaymentIntent and customer email/name/billing address on Customer, and can use Radar Sessions for advanced signals. Elements is recommended with customer factors in the integration table.

Both snapshots give provider estimates of 36% advanced risk factors, 12% IP, 11% email, 3% name and 1% billing address. Integration list order and recommended labels are visible but the right-hand completeness cells are blank in both raws. The capture does not quantify each integration row, establish ranks as measured or establish additive merchant fraud reduction.

Both guides recommend reusing Customer with associated billing address and saved methods for cross-method pattern history, giving email at Customer creation and name when tokenizing, and storing shipping only when physical goods are shipped. They recommend handling declines on manual PaymentIntent creation and tracking repeated attempts if reusing the Intent.

Both advise loading Stripe.js directly from the provider-hosted script across website pages and keeping device/behavior collection in the merchant’s privacy policy. The example and hosted URL change from Dahlia to Endive in November. No Radar behavior or migration result is measured.

Radar scans on a Charge basis and PaymentIntent retries may yield multiple scanned charges. Saving for future use without a charge is excluded by default. A merchant can opt into SetupIntent scanning in the named Radar setting. The setting does not prove successful setup or charge outcome.
substantive_changes: The hosted Stripe.js version reference moves from the May Dahlia path to the November Endive path in both example and direct-loading instruction. Preserve as versioned integration evidence. The Radar inputs, estimates, per-Charge scan semantics, SetupIntent default and practice guidance are unchanged.
historical_claims_to_preserve: May 10 Dahlia and November 7 Endive provider script URLs are dated example guidance. Direct hosted loading and avoiding a local copy recur in both captures.
Preserve 36/12/11/3/1 as provider-estimated model improvement, the three recommended table variants, customer-vs-client object identity, and opt-in saved-for-future-use scanning scope.
conflicts: Mapped source lines 13 and 33–42 and Radar concept line 112 present a measured best-to-worst ranking. Both captures lack rendered completeness values for all eight rows. Preserve order and three explicit recommendations while qualifying the implied ranking.

Mapped source line 47 presents shipping details without the physical-goods condition and line 49 omits the per-Charge and charge-free setup distinction. Radar concept line 114 should keep opt-in explicit. Both raws establish those details independently of the November script reference.
Both index and company route labels call the integration list a ranking. Qualify the available completeness evidence when relinking.
unresolved_questions: Whether the published table rendered completeness values that the snapshots did not capture remains unresolved. The documentation does not prove relative scores or performance for a particular integration.
The URL change does not establish API version, deployment, migration requirement, measured efficacy or SDK behavior outside the referenced version.

findings: Keep the source’s existing data values as provider estimates, qualify the integration list’s blank completeness cells, and preserve dated hosted script guidance, shipping condition, and per-Charge versus charge-free setup scope.
conflicts: The best-to-worst source heading goes beyond the visible cells; the customer and setup bullets compress documented prerequisites and payment versus setup distinctions.
source_assessments.reason: The new capture is chiefly another versioned reference. Corrections to existing summary scope and table evidence are independently supported by both raws.

answers.Q1: At https://docs.stripe.com/radar/optimize-risk-factors, source-stripe-radar-optimize-risk-factors.md summarizes how Stripe Radar evaluates payment data. Old raw lines 8–37 and new raw lines 9–38 distinguish Stripe-collected device signals from Customer identity/address and PaymentIntent client signals the merchant supplies. The recommended integration rows and reported model-improvement estimates remain stable. Old raw lines 43–58 and new raw lines 44–59 recommend Customer continuity across payment methods, shipping information for physical goods and tracking repeats when reusing a PaymentIntent. Old raw lines 76–78 and new raw lines 77–79 say Radar scans per charge, potentially across retries. With no charge at setup, Radar does not scan by default. The merchant can enable SetupIntent scanning in Radar settings.
answers.Q2: At https://docs.stripe.com/radar/optimize-risk-factors, source-stripe-radar-optimize-risk-factors.md should retain old raw lines 60–68 as May Dahlia and new raw lines 61–69 as November Endive hosted script examples and direct-loading instructions. The versioned reference changes while the guidance to collect signals across site pages and load from Stripe remains. Heading, emphasis, table formatting, punctuation and link-label changes are presentation. Old raw lines 16–25 and new raw lines 17–26 mark three rows recommended and have empty completeness cells; qualify the existing best-to-worst claim separately. Retain per-Charge versus charge-free-setup scope from old raw lines 76–78 and new raw lines 77–79. Preserve the reciprocal source route in wiki/concepts/stripe-radar.md and qualify the integration-ranking characterizations in wiki/stripe-index.md and wiki/companies/stripe.md.
